narrative.text:
ENCOUNTER:
On September 14, 2023, at approximately 0640 hours, Border Patrol Agents [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] and [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] were conducting traffic observation duties on Interstate 94 near Kalamazoo, Michigan. The agents conducted a vehicle stop on a white sedan after a records check showed the registered owner had an outstanding immigration matter. The driver, later identified as [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)], presented a valid Michigan driver's license and was determined to be a United States citizen; he was released at the scene. Agent [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] then questioned the passenger, who is the subject of this report, as to his citizenship.
The subject stated that he is a citizen and national of Honduras and that he does not possess any documents allowing him to be in or remain in the United States legally. He further stated that he last entered the United States on or about March 3, 2016, by crossing the Rio Grande on foot near Roma, Texas, and that he was not inspected by an immigration officer. He presented a Honduran national identity card bearing his name.
TRAVEL:
After crossing, the subject travelled by car to Houston, Texas, and later by bus to Kalamazoo, where he has worked in construction.
REMOVABILITY:
The subject is inadmissible under Section 212(a)(6)(A)(i) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, in that he is an alien present in the United States without being admitted or paroled.
DISPOSITION:
The subject was transported to the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] Border Patrol Station, processed, and served a Notice to Appear (Form I-862). He will be held pending removal proceedings.
